new.s: The first passenger railway in India, opened on 16 April 1853, ran between:
new.x: The first passenger train ran from Bombay (Bori Bunder) to Thane (34 km) on 16 April 1853, run by the Great Indian Peninsula Railway. Royapuram-Wallajah Road (1856) was the first line in South India, Puttur-Renigunta (1862) the first in Andhra, and Calcutta-Diamond Harbour was the first telegraph line (1851).

new.s: The first telegraph line in India (1851) connected:
new.x: The first telegraph line ran from Calcutta to Diamond Harbour in 1851, laid under W.B. O'Shaughnessy. Calcutta-Peshawar was part of the trunk network of the mid-1850s, not the first line. Bombay-Thane was the first passenger railway (1853), and Madras-Arcot (Royapuram-Wallajah Road) the first South Indian railway (1856).

new.s: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878, nicknamed the 'Gagging Act', was repealed in 1882 by:
new.x: Lord Ripon repealed the 'Gagging Act' in 1882. Lytton passed it in 1878, Mayo is linked with Section 124A (1870), and Minto II with the press laws of 1908 and 1910.

new.s: To escape the Vernacular Press Act, which newspaper converted itself overnight into an English-language paper in 1878?
new.x: Amrita Bazar Patrika became an English paper overnight because the VPA applied only to Indian-language papers. Som Prakash was a target of the Act. The Hindu was already in English, and Kesari was a Marathi paper.
new.tq: ABP dodged the VPA by switching to English.

new.s: The patronage of the Company's Directors over civil service appointments was abolished, and open competitive examination introduced, by the:
new.x: Appointments were made by the Directors' patronage until 1853. The Charter Act of 1853 replaced patronage with open competition, with support from Trevelyan and Robert Lowe. The 1833 Act came before this change, the 1861 Act let Indians into mainly uncovenanted posts, and the 1858 Act transferred power to the Crown.

new.s: Who was the first Indian to enter the Indian Civil Service?
new.x: Satyendranath Tagore became the first Indian in the ICS in 1864 (many texts say 1863). Ram Mohan Roy, in 1832, was the first to demand Indians in higher posts. Surendranath Banerjea and Dadabhai Naoroji are not the 'first Indian ICS' answer.

new.x: The Cantonments Act of 1924 was passed by the Central legislature (an APPSC-G2 2025 statement). It was not a provincial council's Act or an Act of the British Parliament, and the Royal Commission on Decentralisation (1907-09) only made recommendations.

new.s: Who is known as the 'Father of Local Self-Government in India'?
new.x: Lord Ripon, whose 1882 Resolution is called the Magna Carta of local self-government, is the Father of Local Self-Government. Mayo's 1870 Resolution began financial decentralisation, and Hobhouse chaired the 1907 Royal Commission on Decentralisation. Curzon is not given this title.
new.tq: Ripon 1882 = Father of LSG; Mayo 1870 = financial decentralisation.
